title: Stress Awareness
osha_standards: OSH Act Section 5(a)(1) General Duty Clause
summary: Job stress is the physical and emotional harm that happens when job demands do not match a worker's abilities or resources. It can lead to poor health and injury, so ask for help and watch out for coworkers.
talking_points: Job stress can lead to poor health and even injury. It happens when the demands of the work do not match your abilities or the resources you have.
Ask for help if you feel overwhelmed by the work.
Look out for your coworkers. If one shows signs of stress, offer to help if you can.
Tell your supervisor or your shop steward if the schedule is creating pressure that is affecting your work and health.
Take good care of yourself to reduce stress. Exercise regularly. It is a powerful stress reliever.
See a doctor if you have frequent headaches, cannot sleep, have trouble concentrating, have an upset stomach, or have a short temper.
site_hazards_to_check: Projects behind schedule with crews under heavy pressure to work faster
Workers who seem overwhelmed, withdrawn, or short-tempered
Yelling or blaming on the site instead of problem solving
Workers rushing and cutting corners because of the schedule
No clear way for workers to raise concerns about workload
discussion_questions: How can pressure to hurry affect the quality and safety of our work?
What signs of stress have you seen in yourself or a coworker?
Who can you go to if the schedule or workload is too much?
